Hardware accelerated JPEG decode is available on the following GPUs - A100, A30, H100.
The encoding functions of the nvJPEG library perform GPU-accelerated compression of user’s image data to the JPEG bitstream.
Uses Hardware Acceleration for decode. Supports baseline JPEG images with single scan with 1 or 3 channels. 410 and 411 chroma subsamplings are not supported.

Hardware accelerated JPEG decode is available on the following GPUs architectures - Ampere (A100, A30) Hopper Ada Blackwell Platforms which support hardware accelerated JPEG decode: Windows Linux (x86_64, PowerPC, ARM64) Hardware accelerated JPEG encode is available on Jetson Thor (Blackwell), running Linux ARM64.

NVJPEG_ENC_BACKEND_DEFAULT Use hardware engine if possible. If not, fallback to CUDA encoder. NVJPEG_ENC_BACKEND_GPU Always use CUDA encoder. NVJPEG_ENC_BACKEND_HARDWARE Always use hardware engine. Do not fallback to CUDA.
The encoding functions of the nvJPEG library perform GPU-accelerated compression of user’s image data to the JPEG bitstream.
Added hardware-accelerated JPEG encoding support for NVIDIA Jetson Thor hardware (Blackwell SM 10.1 architecture).
Added hardware-accelerated JPEG decoding support in nvJPEG for NVIDIA Blackwell architecture GPUs.
nvjpegEncode: Replaces nvjpegEncodeYUV and nvjpegEncodeImage. nvjpegEncode is required for hardware encoding
Maxwell, Pascal, and Volta architectures are now feature-complete with no further enhancements planned.

Planar YUV (P_YUV) is not converted, and CPU-only encoders are unaffected.
Encoding a chroma-subsampled Image is not supported yet and raises ValueError.
Added JPEG decoding support for two new formats: NV12 and YUY2, for both hardware engine and CUDA. For NV12, the chroma subsampling must be 420, and for YUY2, it must be 422.
